chunks: And by this chain, from Hammad, from Rib'i, from al-Fuzayl, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:
'From the matters are matters suspended in the presence of God. He brings forward from them whatever He wills, and He delays from them whatever He wills.'

key_terms.أُمُورٌ مَوْقُوفَةٌ: matters suspended/held in abeyance — affairs whose execution God has temporarily withheld
key_terms.الْبَدَاء: al-Bada' — the concept of God's power to alter or 'reveal anew' His plan
key_terms.يُؤَخِّرُ: delays/postpones — God's act of deferring something
key_terms.يُقَدِّمُ: brings forward/advances — God's act of causing something to occur sooner

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about matters suspended with God in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) teaches that God holds certain matters in a state of suspension — not yet decreed as final — and from among these suspended matters, He brings some forward and delays others according to His absolute will. This is a direct elaboration of the doctrine of al-Bada', the concept that God has the power to alter or revise what was previously withheld from execution, affirming His complete and ongoing sovereignty over all affairs. This teaching would have resonated deeply with early Shia Muslims as a theological assertion of divine freedom against fatalistic or predeterminist views.

en.hubeali:
And, by this chain, from Hammad, from Rabie, from Al Fuzayl who said, 
‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying:

‘From the matters is a matter suspended in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. He<sup>azwj</sup> Brings forward from these whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to, and Delays from these whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to’.
